doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Buster Anderson and Bert Russell's dirty blues
summary: Burns and his wife recall pianist Buster Anderson who played blues with Bert Russell.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He played in so long piano.
He played in so long. He played in so long. He played in so long.
He used to call them Tunk. Buster Anderson's blues too. I used to play them.
Did Buster Anderson play with my uncle and him?
Oh, sure he played with Bert Russel and him sometimes. Yeah, well then that was the piano man. See I couldn't remember the name. Did you get, you give him Bert Russel?
Yeah. Buster Anderson was a piano player. Yeah.
Yeah. Well Buster Anderson was, that's right.
It used to be Buster, that's what it was. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Buster Anderson played with Marcel and Russel. Yeah. And they played blues like this? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Some dirty ones in me. Yeah. They were playing them before me.
Yeah. They tried to play a dirty one. I forgot. I don't play, you see.
You know I never touch this piano. But still you can remember them and I got a very good idea how it sounded. Really very interesting, your left hand. Yeah. It is.
